raw_plan.interpretation: Create one acquisition email for the selected audience, narrowed in line with the current dossier to national and devolved government digital teams. The email should introduce Plausible as a product worth evaluating, not assume the reader currently uses Google Analytics, and earn a bounded first evaluation rather than an immediate deployment.

intent.reason_now: Public-sector analytics choices must support performance measurement while giving Information Governance and DPIA reviewers concrete answers about cookies, personal data and data residency.
intent.desired_action: View Plausible's live example dashboard and decide whether the product merits a formal privacy and reporting evaluation.

raw_plan.reader: A national or devolved government digital team assessing whether a web analytics product can provide useful performance data while meeting its privacy-governance requirements.
raw_plan.reader_segment: An EU or UK public sector web team that must publish analytics without a consent banner
raw_plan.reader_scope: National and devolved government digital teams only; do not generalize the fit to every EU or UK public-sector organization.
raw_plan.promise: Plausible offers a documented no-cookie, no-personal-data analytics approach with EU-only visitor-data processing that a public-sector team can assess before beginning a formal adoption process.
raw_plan.orientation: Plausible is a hosted web analytics product whose documentation gives public-sector reviewers concrete answers about cookies, identifiable visitor data and EU data processing.
raw_plan.arc: Move the reader from general product awareness to one bounded decision: whether Plausible's privacy design and dashboard warrant a formal Information Governance and reporting evaluation.
raw_plan.sequence_rationale: Because there is only one email, it must stand alone. It leads with the audience's defining eligibility question, supports the claim with a concrete privacy mechanism and EU-processing detail, and asks for a read-only look at the live dashboard. It does not assume an installed analytics stack, claim legal approval or ask the reader to deploy tracking before deciding whether deeper evaluation is worthwhile.

emails.selection_reason: Cookie use, identifiable visitor data and data residency are threshold questions for this audience. Plausible has specific, checkable documentation on all three, so the email can give the reader a concrete reason to evaluate it without inventing a current vendor, migration project or past failure.
emails.job: Earn a visit to the live example dashboard so the reader can decide whether Plausible merits a formal privacy and reporting review.
emails.single_idea: Plausible is worth evaluating because its analytics design uses no cookies, does not collect personal data about visitors and keeps visitor-data processing within the EU, giving a public-sector review team concrete claims and mechanisms to assess.
emails.mechanism: Plausible documents that it requires no cookies or personal-data collection. It creates a daily-changing identifier by hashing the visitor's IP address and User-Agent with a rotating salt, while visitor data is processed exclusively on servers owned and operated by European companies and does not leave the EU.

alternative_arguments.selection_reason: A privacy-qualified tool still has to support public performance reporting. This alternative gives the reader a different reason to act by making the available reporting functions and their plan boundaries explicit before a technical evaluation begins.
alternative_arguments.single_idea: Plausible can be evaluated as a no-cookie analytics option without treating it as top-line traffic reporting only: the Business plan includes funnels, user journeys and Data Studio, while scheduled event- and session-level exports are reserved for Enterprise.
alternative_arguments.mechanism: Plausible's documented no-cookie and no-personal-data design remains the eligibility foundation. For reporting depth, Business adds funnels, user journeys and Data Studio; organizations that require scheduled event- and session-level data in their own S3-compatible storage would need Enterprise.
alternative_arguments.belief_shift: Before: a privacy-oriented analytics product may be too limited for a government reporting workflow. After: Plausible has documented reporting routes worth comparing, with important plan boundaries that can be checked before evaluation.
must_not_say: Do not claim Plausible reproduces GA4, BigQuery or Looker Studio workflows.
Do not claim the reporting features will answer every stakeholder question.
Do not imply that funnels, user journeys or Data Studio are available below the Business plan.
Do not imply that raw event data exports are available outside Enterprise.
Do not claim setup, migration or procurement will be quick or easy.
Do not present the no-cookie statement as independent legal certification or automatic regulatory approval.
alternative_arguments.objection: A privacy-oriented analytics product may not provide enough reporting depth for the questions the team must answer.
alternative_arguments.next_step_decision: Decide whether the documented Business or Enterprise reporting routes are sufficient to justify a deeper technical evaluation.
alternative_arguments.next_step_value: Compare the plan boundary for funnels, user journeys and Data Studio, and see that scheduled event- and session-level exports require Enterprise.
alternative_arguments.next_step_limit: The pricing comparison does not prove that Plausible covers the team's specific reporting schema, data volumes, procurement requirements or production workflow.
alternative_arguments.subject_strategy: Frame the open around reporting depth with an honest plan boundary, not around generic simplicity or an unsupported claim that Plausible replaces the reader's current analytics stack.

emails.belief_shift: Before: Plausible is another privacy-friendly analytics claim that would still require substantial qualification. After: its cookie, identifier and EU-processing design is specific enough to justify a closer evaluation.
must_not_say: Do not claim every EU or UK public-sector organization is an established fit; the supported scope is national and devolved government digital teams.
Do not assert that the recipient currently uses Google Analytics, GA4, Google Tag Manager, Matomo or any other named tool.
Do not say the recipient has already experienced reporting failures, migration problems or consent-banner costs.
Do not present Plausible's statements as a certification, binding legal opinion, guaranteed GDPR compliance or automatic consent exemption.
Do not claim that adopting Plausible alone authorizes removal of an existing consent banner; the team's Information Governance and legal review remains its own decision.
Do not promise setup effort, migration time, procurement speed, savings or a complete replacement for an existing analytics stack.
Do not add pricing, customer logos, uptime, trial terms, security controls or reporting-feature lists to this primary argument.
Do not imply that the live demo proves production fit, internal approval or legal compliance.
emails.objection: A high-level privacy claim is not enough for an Information Governance or DPIA review.
emails.tone: Matter-of-fact, precise and respectful of formal review responsibilities.
emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether Plausible's dashboard and documented privacy model warrant a formal Information Governance and reporting evaluation.
emails.next_step_value: See a live example dashboard before committing to account creation or implementation, with the no-cookie and no-personal-data design as the reason for considering it.
emails.next_step_limit: The demo does not establish legal compliance, consent-exemption eligibility, internal DPIA approval, procurement suitability or coverage of the team's production reporting requirements.
emails.subject_strategy: Name the assessable privacy distinction—analytics without cookies or personal-data collection—without promising legal approval or using a generic privacy-first slogan.

raw_plan.voice_notes: Use public-sector review language such as Information Governance and DPIA sparingly. Attribute compliance-sensitive statements to Plausible's documented design rather than presenting them as independent legal conclusions. Keep the email short, declarative and free of hype.

events.subject: Evaluate analytics without cookies
events.preview_text: Inspect Plausible’s dashboard and documented approach before starting a formal review.
events.body:
See what cookie-free web analytics would give your team before opening a formal review. Plausible Analytics is a web analytics tool with a live example dashboard you can inspect without creating an account.

For an Information Governance or DPIA assessment, the design is specific: Plausible documents that it uses no cookies and collects no personal data about visitors.

To calculate daily unique visitor numbers, it hashes the visitor’s IP address and User-Agent with a rotating salt. The identifier changes daily, and the raw IP address and User-Agent are never written to disk.

Visitor data is processed exclusively on EU servers owned and operated by European companies. The live dashboard lets you assess the reporting experience alongside that documented privacy model, then decide whether a formal evaluation is warranted.

events.message: Email 1, draft 1: "Reporting depth, with clear boundaries"
events.subject: Reporting depth, with clear boundaries
events.preview_text: Compare Business reporting features with Enterprise data exports.
events.body:
Plausible Analytics is web analytics software documented to use no cookies and collect no personal data. Its reporting depth is defined by plan.

Business includes funnels and user journeys for examining fixed paths through a service. It also includes Data Studio for building custom dashboards and blending Plausible data with other sources.

The boundary is clear. Scheduled exports of event- and session-level data are Enterprise-only, delivered daily to your organisation’s S3-compatible object storage.

The plans page lets you compare those reporting routes before deciding whether Plausible merits a deeper Information Governance, DPIA and technical evaluation.

events.subject: What Plausible processes each day
events.preview_text: See the documented mechanism behind its no-cookie analytics model.
events.body:
A no-cookie claim is easy to make. The underlying data handling is what a governance review needs to examine.

Plausible Analytics provides web analytics without cookies. Its documented position is that it collects no personal data about visitors and requires no consent banner.

Its Security documentation explains the mechanism: an IP address and User-Agent are hashed with a rotating salt to create an identifier that changes daily. Plausible also states that visitor data is processed exclusively on EU servers owned and operated by European companies.

The supporting Data Policy, Security documentation, privacy policy and data processing agreement are indexed at plausible.io/compliance. They provide the technical and legal material for your team’s own assessment; they are not a certification or legal conclusion.

The live example dashboard separately shows the reporting experience, without requiring account creation or implementation. Inspect it to decide whether Plausible warrants a formal privacy and reporting evaluation.
